mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within two months signals economic weakness, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where UNRATE increases by more than 0.5% within two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate sales (HOUST) over three months signals a strengthening economy, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where HOUST shows a sustained increase over three months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within two months signals a supply-side contraction, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where INDPRO decreases by more than 1% within two months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 2% over the previous quarter signals strong economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where GDPC1 increases by more than 2% over the previous quarter.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4.5% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure and tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary period with high interest rates
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2%, it signals a tightening labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month and UNRATE decreases > 0.2%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 and UNRATE decreases by more than 0.2% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% within two months signals a weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where RSAFS decreases by more than 1% within two months.
